description: Repair the sandbox executor git recovery path in apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/entrypoint/executor.py. After the coding agent finishes, executor.py probes the cloned workspace with 'git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree'. When that probe fails it currently deletes the workspace .git directory, runs 'git init', pins HEAD with 'git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/<exec_branch>' and re-adds the origin remote. No fetch, reset or update-ref step ever re-attaches the base plan_branch commit, so the execution commit is created as an orphan root commit and the pushed execution branch shares no history with plan_branch or main. Deleting .git outright also destroys the object database and refs that were still present in the sandbox at that moment.
goal: Make the git recovery path non-destructive and history-preserving. 1) Diagnose and handle the benign causes of a failing 'git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree' probe first (for example an unrecognised safe.directory ownership error, a transient lock, or a GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_DIR environment override left behind by the agent runner) so that a healthy repository is never rebuilt: repair or work around them and continue with the existing repository. 2) Never delete a .git directory that still contains a usable object database; if the repository must be recovered, keep the existing .git, and when it is genuinely unusable move it aside to a timestamped backup path inside the workspace instead of calling shutil.rmtree. 3) When re-initialising, re-attach the base commit before staging: add the origin remote, fetch the plan_branch (honouring a configurable refspec/retry count), then point HEAD at the recovered branch and reset --soft (or use git update-ref) onto the fetched base commit so subsequent 'git add' and 'git commit' produce a commit whose parent is the plan_branch tip. 4) Fail loud instead of silently producing an orphan commit: if the base commit cannot be recovered, log an actionable error, mark the execution as failed in the ledger, and skip the push of the orphan branch, while still preserving the execution record and workspace diagnostics. 5) Update the misleading assertion in apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_executor.py (the existing test only asserts that a 'git symbolic-ref HEAD' command was issued, which locks in the defective behaviour) and add regression tests that simulate an invalid or missing .git after agent execution and assert that the resulting execution commit has the plan_branch tip as its parent, that no rmtree of a usable .git occurs, and that the codebase files plus executions/*.md and holon-knowledge/ledger/executions.jsonl are all present in the resulting commit. Keep the change confined to apps/sandbox-executor, follow the repository Python, linting and test conventions, and make sure the full sandbox-executor test suite passes.
